item.title: NEW: Microsoft Patches Actively Exploited Outlook Zero-Day in Massive Update
item.description:
Headline: Microsoft Patches Actively Exploited Outlook Zero-Day in Massive Update

Summary:
Microsoft's November 2026 Patch Tuesday addressed over 1,200 vulnerabilities, including a critical zero-day in Outlook, CVE-2026-124194, which is being actively exploited. The flaw allows attackers to steal NTLM authentication hashes by tricking users into opening a malicious message file. The vulnerability does not trigger in the Preview Pane, requiring direct user interaction. In response, CISA has added CVE-2026-124194 to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog, mandating federal agencies to patch by November 24, 2026.

Severity: High

Categories: Patch Management, Vulnerability, Phishing

Article Type: Advisory

Meta Description: Microsoft's November 2026 Patch Tuesday fixes an actively exploited Outlook zero-day, CVE-2026-124194, that allows for NTLM hash theft via malicious .msg files.

item.title: NEW: France Blames Iran-Backed Group for Sabotaging 700+ Supermarket Refrigerators
item.description:
Headline: France Blames Iran-Backed Group for Sabotaging 700+ Supermarket Refrigerators

Summary:
French and U.S. authorities have attributed a large-scale sabotage campaign against over 700 European supermarkets to SHAHID KAVEH, an Iranian state-backed group affiliated with the IRGC. The attackers remotely compromised and manipulated industrial refrigeration controllers, causing tens of millions of euros in damages from food spoilage and equipment fires. The attacks exploited exposed web interfaces on controllers from brands like Danfoss and Copeland. France has condemned the incident as a destructive act of sabotage and is pursuing EU-level sanctions.

Severity: Critical

Categories: Cyberattack, Industrial Control Systems, Threat Actor

Article Type: NewsArticle

Meta Description: An Iran-backed hacking group, SHAHID KAVEH, is blamed for a destructive sabotage attack on over 700 European supermarkets by manipulating refrigeration controllers.

item.title: NEW: N-able Takes N-central RMM Offline After 30+ Zero-Days Publicly Disclosed
item.description:
Headline: N-able Takes N-central RMM Offline After 30+ Zero-Days Publicly Disclosed

Summary:
IT software provider N-able was forced to take its hosted N-central RMM platform offline globally after a security researcher publicly disclosed over 30 zero-day vulnerabilities, dubbed 'Able2Shell.' The flaws, which include critical bugs leading to unauthenticated remote code execution, were published with proof-of-concept exploits. N-able has since released an emergency hotfix, 2026.4 HF2, and is advising all on-premises customers to patch immediately due to the severe supply chain risk posed to managed service providers (MSPs).

Severity: Critical

Categories: Vulnerability, Supply Chain Attack, Patch Management

Article Type: Advisory

Meta Description: N-able issued an emergency hotfix for its N-central RMM platform after a researcher disclosed over 30 zero-day vulnerabilities, dubbed 'Able2Shell,' online.

item.title: NEW: Blind Eagle APT Uses HTML Smuggling to Target Latin American Entities
item.description:
Headline: Blind Eagle APT Uses HTML Smuggling to Target Latin American Entities

Summary:
The Spanish-speaking APT group Blind Eagle (APT-C-36) has launched a new espionage campaign targeting government, judicial, and financial entities in Latin America, with a focus on Colombia. The operation uses sophisticated spear-phishing emails with judicial themes that employ HTML smuggling to deliver a malicious ZIP archive, bypassing email security gateways. The final payload is a custom remote access trojan (RAT), derived from AsyncRAT, capable of data exfiltration and keystroke logging.

Severity: High

Categories: Threat Actor, Phishing, Malware

Article Type: NewsArticle

Meta Description: The Blind Eagle (APT-C-36) threat group is using sophisticated phishing lures and HTML smuggling to target entities in Latin America with a custom remote access trojan.

item.title: NEW: CISA Adds Six Actively Exploited Flaws to 'Must-Patch' KEV Catalog
item.description:
Headline: CISA Adds Six Actively Exploited Flaws to 'Must-Patch' KEV Catalog

Summary:
On November 10, 2026, the U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) added six new vulnerabilities to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog, indicating they are under active attack. The list includes critical flaws in products from Microsoft, Cisco, Barracuda, Google, and Openwave. Federal agencies are mandated to patch these vulnerabilities by specified deadlines, and CISA urges all organizations to prioritize their remediation to reduce exposure to active threats.

Severity: Critical

Categories: Patch Management, Vulnerability, Regulatory

item.title: NEW: Vanderbilt University Hit by BYOD Ransomware; Attackers Claim Massive Data Theft
item.description:
Headline: Vanderbilt University Hit by BYOD Ransomware; Attackers Claim Massive Data Theft

Summary:
Vanderbilt University is recovering from a major ransomware attack claimed by the 'BYOD' group, which began on November 9, 2026. The incident caused widespread system disruptions, forcing the university to shut down devices and network access. The BYOD gang alleges it exfiltrated a massive trove of data, including over one million Social Security numbers, student records, and research data. While Vanderbilt has begun restoring services, it has not confirmed the data theft claims. The attack follows a pattern of the BYOD group targeting higher education and healthcare.

Severity: High

Categories: Ransomware, Data Breach, Cyberattack

Article Type: NewsArticle

Meta Description: The BYOD ransomware gang has claimed a major cyberattack against Vanderbilt University, alleging the theft of over one million Social Security numbers and causing system-wide disruptions.

item.title: NEW: Fireworks AI Breach Widens, Exposing Billing Data and Models via Cloud Provider Hack
item.description:
Headline: Fireworks AI Breach Widens, Exposing Billing Data and Models via Cloud Provider Hack

Summary:
AI startup Fireworks AI has revealed its October 2026 data breach was more severe than initially reported, involving a second incident where attackers pivoted from a compromised third-party cloud provider. A financially motivated group stole customer billing data and incomplete AI models in an attack linked to 'LLMjacking.' The breach also impacted downstream customers, including Notion, which confirmed some of its AI chat transcripts may have been accessed.

Severity: High

Categories: Data Breach, Supply Chain Attack, Cloud Security

item.title: NEW: North Korean APT Kimsuky Linked to "Trigram" Espionage Campaign
item.description:
Headline: North Korean APT Kimsuky Linked to "Trigram" Espionage Campaign

Summary:
A cyber-espionage operation named the 'Trigram' campaign has been attributed to the North Korean threat group Kimsuky (APT-43). The campaign targets organizations in the AI, blockchain, and logistics sectors in Europe and the U.S. Attackers use social engineering, primarily fake job offers, to lure software developers into a multi-stage infection process that delivers an information-stealing malware. The operation highlights North Korea's persistent focus on intelligence gathering and revenue generation from technology sectors.

Severity: High

Categories: Threat Actor, Phishing, Malware

Article Type: NewsArticle

item.title: UPDATE: Vanderbilt University Hit by 'BYOD' Ransomware, Over 1M Records at Risk
item.description:
Headline: Vanderbilt University Hit by 'BYOD' Ransomware, Over 1M Records at Risk

Summary:
Vanderbilt University has confirmed a major cybersecurity incident, identified as a ransomware attack by the 'BYOD' group. The attackers claim to have stolen sensitive data, including Social Security numbers, for over one million students and staff. The university's IT department instructed campus members to disconnect from Wi-Fi as it works to contain the breach, which has disrupted campus systems and encrypted files with a '.byod' extension.

Severity: High

Categories: Ransomware, Data Breach, Cyberattack

Meta Description: Vanderbilt University confirms a major ransomware attack by the 'BYOD' group, which claims to have stolen data on over one million students and staff.
